title: The Carnival of Broken Dreams
description: A traveling night-market of tents, music, and miracles glides the trade-roads between Silkstrand and Thepyrgos. It grants wishes—precisely—and charges a price in things people didn't know they valued. As the Desire Index rises, a town's intangibles unravel: lullabies vanish, bell-rights lapse, markets drift off schedule. The party can expose terms, retune the engine, or divert its appetite before the carnival moves on.
author: Nicholas A. Gasper

bestiary.name: Maestra Pann
bestiary.description: The ringmaster of the Carnival of Broken Dreams. She speaks with velvet coaxing, bell cues, and a relentless focus on spectacle. She is not evil—she is the carnival's heart, and its prisoner. The calliope chose her, and she cannot leave.

sb_spends.name: Change the Beat
sb_spends.effect: The scene's rhythm shifts; all actions become Desperate for one exchange.

sb_spends.name: Elevate the Stakes
sb_spends.effect: A public spectacle demands a sacrifice; one PC must offer something or lose a Boon.

sb_spends.name: Flatter a Rival
sb_spends.effect: A rival NPC becomes compliant for one scene, but gains a String on the flatterer.

bestiary.lore: She did not choose this life. The calliope chose her. Two-finger bell count before a hard turn.
bestiary.secret: She is the carnival's heart—and its prisoner. She has tried to leave three times. The calliope always calls her back.

bestiary.name: Mr. Vellum
bestiary.description: The carnival's ledger-clerk. A papery whisper of a man with ink under his nails. He balances the books—on his own terms. He was once a Silkstrand notary who made a wish he couldn't afford.

sb_spends.name: Correct the Contract
sb_spends.effect: A contract gains a hidden clause; one PC is bound until they discover it.

sb_spends.name: Split the Cost
sb_spends.effect: The price of a wish is divided among bystanders; the party must choose who bears it.

sb_spends.name: Misfile Your Name
sb_spends.effect: A PC's name is lost in the ledgers; they cannot prove their identity for one scene.

bestiary.lore: He checks his quill nib before lying. He writes the carnival's prices in negative space—only those who know where to look can read them.
bestiary.secret: He was a Silkstrand notary who made a wish he couldn't afford. Now he writes the carnival's prices to pay the debt.

bestiary.name: The Cotton Witch
bestiary.description: A Livaea-touched enchantress with sugared lips and cravings-as-magic. She feeds your appetite until you consent to anything. She hums when you hesitate.

sb_spends.name: Sweet Trial
sb_spends.effect: Offer a minor wish; the taker must test Spirit or gain a Compulsion.

sb_spends.name: Mirror Your Desire
sb_spends.effect: She reflects a PC's deepest want back at them; they act at Desperate until they resist.

sb_spends.name: Name Your Envy
sb_spends.effect: She names a PC's secret envy aloud; the PC loses 1 Boon unless they confess.

bestiary.lore: She was once a Thepyrgos academic who craved popularity. The carnival gave her an audience that never leaves. She hums when you hesitate.
bestiary.secret: She was once a Thepyrgos academic who craved popularity. The carnival gave her an audience that never leaves—but she cannot leave either.

bestiary.name: Harlequin of Courts
bestiary.description: Mab's envoy to the carnival. They enforce order, pretty rules, and public victories. They bow before cuts, and they serve a court that demands obedience.

sb_spends.name: Demand Apology
sb_spends.effect: A PC must apologize or be marked by the Court; -1 die to social rolls until they do.

sb_spends.name: Set a Forfeit
sb_spends.effect: A contest is declared; the loser must offer a String or a Boon.

sb_spends.name: Bind to Theater
sb_spends.effect: A PC is compelled to play a role; they cannot act against that role for the scene.

bestiary.lore: They bow before cuts. They are not cruel—they serve a court that demands obedience.
bestiary.secret: They are not truly cruel—they serve a court that demands obedience, and the carnival is their only escape from endless etiquette.

bestiary.name: The Ticket Twins
bestiary.description: The carnival's ushers. Synchronized blinks, bright patter, and a relentless focus on throughput and safety theater. They are the carnival's children—foundlings raised in the tents.

sb_spends.name: Reassign Seating
sb_spends.effect: The party is separated; one PC cannot assist another for the scene.

sb_spends.name: Isolate Meddlers
sb_spends.effect: A PC is surrounded by staff; they act at Desperate until they escape.

sb_spends.name: Edit Consent
sb_spends.effect: A contract is 'checked' after signing; the terms have changed.

bestiary.lore: Synchronized blinks before speaking. They have never known a world without the calliope.
bestiary.secret: They are the carnival's children—foundlings raised in the tents. They have never known a world without the calliope.

bestiary.name: Carnival Staff
bestiary.description: Generic carnival workers. They keep the show running, manage crowds, and enforce the carnival's rules—such as they are.

sb_spends.name: Crowd Control
sb_spends.effect: The staff redirects the crowd; one PC is separated from the group.

acts.title: Act I — Firelight
acts.description: The carnival parade arrives; a 'free wish' hooks an important NPC. The party sees a miracle, then discovers the missing price. Gain your first Diamond (Witness Seal) through a fair-game contest or etiquette duel.

scenes.title: The Firelight Parade
scenes.description: Lanterns, brass, thrilled hush. The carnival arrives with a parade of wonders. A free raffle-wish is 'won' by a sympathetic NPC. Staff 'clarifies' nothing. The crowd is entranced. Something is wrong.

outcomes.clean: You see the miracle clearly and notice something missing. Gain a clue about the Desire Tax.
outcomes.partial: You see the miracle, but the price is hidden. Tick Desire Index +1.
outcomes.miss: You are caught up in the wonder. Tick Desire Index +2 and Community Unraveling +1.

scenes.title: The Witness Seal
scenes.description: To expose the carnival's terms, you must win a Witness Seal—a Diamond that compels staff to name the exact price aloud. Compete in a fair-game or etiquette duel to earn it.

timers.name: Spotlight Heat
timers.description: How targeted the party is by staff

outcomes.clean: You win the Witness Seal. Staff must name prices aloud. Gain Diamond: Witness Seal.
outcomes.partial: You win, but the contest draws attention. Tick Spotlight Heat +1.
outcomes.miss: You lose the contest. You must find another way.

scenes.title: Firelight Fallout
scenes.description: The first wish has been granted. The price is being collected. The community is beginning to fray. The party must decide how to proceed.

acts.title: Act II — Mirrors & Ledgers
acts.description: Investigate the carnival's tents, negotiate terms, steal leverage from the Ledger Wagon, and win Diamonds to constrain predation. Visit the House of Honest Mirrors, the Wishwright's Tent, and the Ledger Wagon.

scenes.title: House of Honest Mirrors
scenes.description: The mirrors show visitors as they believe themselves to be—and hold their price ledger. Break a mirror under Mirror Warrant to read its ledger safely. Each test without refusal ticks Desire Index +1.

outcomes.clean: You read the ledger without triggering the mirror. Gain a Mirror Warrant.
outcomes.partial: You read the ledger, but the mirror shatters. Tick Spotlight Heat +1.
outcomes.miss: The mirror shards animate and reassign masks mid-scene. Tick Spotlight Heat +2.

scenes.title: The Wishwright's Tent
scenes.description: Velvet-law negotiation. Staff 'assumes the difference' unless you have leverage. Divination finds missing clauses but attracts Livaea-touched attendants.

outcomes.clean: You negotiate favorable terms. Gain a Stage Permit.
outcomes.partial: You make progress, but the Wishwright gains an advantage. Tick Carnival Appetite +1.
outcomes.miss: The negotiation fails. Tick Desire Index +1.

scenes.title: The Ledger Wagon Heist
scenes.description: The carnival's traveling records office. Prices are written as negative space on vellum. Copying a ledger grants leverage to unwind a price—but the reader temporarily loses a related social grace.

outcomes.clean: You copy the ledger. Gain leverage to unwind a price.
outcomes.partial: You copy the ledger, but you lose a social grace temporarily.
outcomes.miss: You are caught. Tick Spotlight Heat +2 and Carnival Appetite +1.

acts.title: Act III — The Calliope Heart
acts.description: A public performance powers the engine. Break one pillar—Rhythm, Mask Index, or Ticket Chain—to starve it or retool it. Choose an ending: Expose & Regulate, Starve the Engine, or Divert the Appetite.

scenes.title: The Performance
scenes.description: The calliope plays. The engine feeds on the crowd's desire. The three pillars are vulnerable: Rhythm (crowd cadence), Mask Index (who plays which role), and Ticket Chain (consent tokens).

outcomes.clean: You break the rhythm. The engine staggers.
outcomes.partial: You disrupt the rhythm, but the engine adapts. Tick Carnival Appetite +1.
outcomes.miss: The rhythm overwhelms you. Tick Carnival Appetite +2.

outcomes.clean: You scramble the masks. The engine loses its anchor.
outcomes.partial: You scramble some masks, but others remain in place. Tick Carnival Appetite +1.
outcomes.miss: The masks turn on you. Tick Spotlight Heat +2.

outcomes.clean: You break the consent chain. The engine starves.
outcomes.partial: You break part of the chain. The engine weakens.
outcomes.miss: The chain tightens around you. Tick Carnival Appetite +2.

scenes.title: Ending: Expose & Regulate
scenes.description: The carnival stays—but all wishes require informed, spoken terms. Unraveling clears. Livaea's devotees take interest in you.

outcomes.clean: The carnival agrees to fair terms. Community Unraveling clears.
outcomes.partial: The carnival agrees to some terms. Unraveling reduces but doesn't clear.
outcomes.miss: The carnival rejects your terms. Tick Community Unraveling +2.

scenes.title: Ending: Starve the Engine
scenes.description: Break a pillar. The tents collapse. Debts become letters and must be hand-delivered back to their owners.

outcomes.clean: The engine starves. The carnival dissolves.
outcomes.partial: The engine starves, but some debts remain unresolved.
outcomes.miss: The engine fights back. You must escape.

scenes.title: Ending: Divert the Appetite
scenes.description: Offer a greater, voluntary group vow. The carnival leaves on a promise and returns when it matures. The debt is deferred—but not forgotten.

outcomes.clean: The carnival accepts your vow. It leaves on a promise.
outcomes.partial: The carnival accepts, but your vow has a hidden cost.
outcomes.miss: The carnival rejects your vow. Tick Carnival Appetite +2.

locations.name: The Carnival Grounds
locations.description: A traveling night-market of tents, music, and miracles. The grounds shift each night—the same attractions, but the layout changes. The calliope plays constantly, a song that worms into your dreams.

locations.name: The Firelight Parade
locations.description: The opening spectacle. Lanterns, brass, thrilled hush. The parade marches through the town's main square, drawing the crowd into the carnival's embrace.

locations.name: The House of Honest Mirrors
locations.description: A tent filled with mirrors that show visitors as they believe themselves to be—and hold their price ledger. Each mirror is a contract, waiting to be read.

locations.name: The Wishwright's Tent
locations.description: Velvet-law negotiation. The Wishwright offers wishes at a price. The terms are never quite clear. Leather-bound books hold the carnival's hidden clauses.

locations.name: The Ledger Wagon
locations.description: The carnival's traveling records office. Prices are written as negative space on vellum—you can only read them by holding the page to the light. The wagon is guarded by the Ticket Twins.

locations.name: The Calliope Heart
locations.description: Beneath the main stage, the engine of desire. Three pillars power it: Rhythm (crowd cadence), Mask Index (roles), and Ticket Chain (consent tokens). The heart beats with the crowd's longing.

factions.name: The Carnival Staff
factions.goals: Keep the show running, grow the desire index, feed the calliope
factions.relationship: The staff are not evil—they are trapped. The calliope feeds on desire, and they are its keepers.

factions.name: Devotees of Livaea (Desire)
factions.goals: Feed desire, spread the carnival's influence, find new wishes to grant
factions.relationship: The Cotton Witch is Livaea-touched. They see the carnival as a temple to desire.

factions.name: Mab's Envoys (Etiquette)
factions.goals: Enforce proper conduct, ensure the show proceeds with due ceremony
factions.relationship: The Harlequin of Courts serves Mab. They are not cruel—they are simply bound to the mask.

campaignTimers.name: Desire Index
campaignTimers.description: Each granted wish (+1), heavy crowd teaser (+1 if unopposed). Price magnitude escalates with the index.

campaignTimers.name: Community Unraveling
campaignTimers.description: Any wish taken without informed terms (+1), public goods priced (+1). Customs, names, and bonds fray.

campaignTimers.name: Carnival Appetite
campaignTimers.description: Each botched sabotage the engine can 'eat' (+1), retuning misfire (+1). When full, the carnival performs its grand act.

campaignTimers.name: Spotlight Heat
campaignTimers.description: Public confrontations, breaking taboos, or humiliating staff (+1). How targeted the party is by staff.

notes: This adventure leans on core Fate's Edge procedures: Position & DV (earn leverage first), Timers (visible pressure), SB spends (on 1s), and Diamonds (codified outcomes). The Desire Tax custom procedure: every fulfilled wish costs something the wisher didn't know they valued. As more wishes accrue, the Desire Index rises and prices escalate. The party can expose terms, retune the engine, or divert its appetite before the carnival moves on.

pacing.act1: Describe only symptoms of the carnival's effects: people forgetting songs, losing affection, markets drifting. Never mention the 'engine,' 'three pillars,' or 'Calliope Heart.' If players ask about the carnival's magic, have NPCs point toward the Ledger Wagon or House of Mirrors as places where answers might be found. NPCs are witnesses to what they have seen or lost, not expositors of the carnival's internal logic.
pacing.act2: Allow players to discover the ledger system, the negative-space prices, and the Wishwright's terms. The Cotton Witch and Mr. Vellum can hint at something 'beneath the stage' but should not describe it mechanically. Maestra Pann may appear confident and in control—do not reveal her imprisonment yet.
pacing.act3: The engine and its three pillars (Rhythm, Mask Index, Ticket Chain) become fully visible and actionable here. NPCs can now speak plainly about the machinery. Maestra Pann's imprisonment can be revealed. All mechanical secrets are now fair game.

npcSecrets.maestra-pann: Do not reveal she is a prisoner of the calliope until Act III. In Acts I-II, present her as a confident, commanding ringmaster. She may hint at 'the weight of the show' but never explicitly say she cannot leave.
npcSecrets.mr-vellum: His past as a Silkstrand notary who made a wish he couldn't afford is a clue players can discover via investigation (e.g., reading the Ledger Wagon or questioning him directly). Do not offer this freely in Act I. He is simply 'the ledger-clerk' until players dig deeper.
npcSecrets.cotton-witch: Her origin as a Thepyrgos academic who craved popularity is a tragic backstory, not a front-facing threat. In Acts I-II, she is the 'sugared enchantress' who feeds desire. Her academic past should only surface if players research her or push her emotionally.
npcSecrets.harlequin-courts: Their secret—that they serve Mab and the carnival is their only escape from endless etiquette—is a sympathetic vulnerability. Do not reveal this unless players earn their trust or witness a moment of private exhaustion.
npcSecrets.ticket-twins: Their origin as foundlings raised in the tents is not a secret to hide, but it's also not something they volunteer. They have never known a world without the calliope; this colors their worldview. Reveal it naturally if the party forms a bond with them.

forbiddenEarlyRevelations: The three pillars (Rhythm, Mask Index, Ticket Chain)
Maestra Pann is trapped by the carnival / cannot leave
The engine is powered by desire / runs on wishes
